tldr: The paper introduces Multi-Agent Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (MARFT), a novel paradigm for fine-tuning LLM-based multi-agent systems using adapted reinforcement learning techniques that account for the unique characteristics of LaMAS.
contributions: Proposes MARFT as a LaMAS-oriented formulation of Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
Introduces Flex-MG, a new game model aligned with LaMAS optimization in real-world applications
Provides a universal algorithmic framework tailored for LaMAS with modular and adaptable design
methods: The authors develop MARFT by extending single-agent Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) to multi-agent settings, accounting for asynchronous agent interactions, profile-aware agent design, and heterogeneous architectural configurations inherent to LaMAS. They introduce Flex-MG as a game model suited for LaMAS and build a scalable MARFT framework with a robust core algorithm. The framework is empirically validated through experiments on DeepScaler and DeepCoder, with comparisons to Independent PPO (MAPoRL) and ablations on role specification.
results: Experiments were conducted on DeepScaler and DeepCoder benchmarks, including comparisons with MAPoRL (Independent PPO) and ablation studies on role specification. The framework demonstrated modularity and adaptability for LaMAS training.
limitations: Sample inefficiency remains a challenge when applying RL to LLM-based agents
Dynamic environment modeling is an open problem for MARFT
Current lack of cohesive frameworks specifically designed for LLM-based multi-agent systems in dynamic environments with agentic tasks
Direct application of conventional MARL methods to LaMAS introduces significant challenges due to unique characteristics of LLM-based agents
